fixes.explanation: No gifts in this scene, friend. The text doesn't mention any. What it says is that they “…bowed down before him with their faces to the ground.” (Genesis 42:6) They came to buy grain, and the man selling it was Joseph, the ruler of the land. Bowing is the first thing the verse shows them doing.

Judah's a fair guess, friend, but he isn't the one speaking here. The text gives this line to Reuben: “Didn’t I tell you not to sin against the boy? But you would not listen.” (Genesis 42:22) I think this is a heavy moment, with years of regret coming out all at once.

Levi isn't the one speaking in this scene, friend. Verse 22 says Reuben responded, “Didn’t I tell you not to sin against the boy?” (Genesis 42:22) I think this one hurts. Reuben is reminding them that he warned them, and now they have to account for what happened.

problems.problem: The passage does not say the brothers arrived with empty sacks or that they had a long list of worries.
Judah is not named in this passage. Saying he is in the family brings in a fact from elsewhere without a reference.
Levi is not named in this passage. Identifying him as one of the brothers brings in a fact from elsewhere without a reference.
